about: General Technic mechanisms. Each set's mechanisms.json uses these types. Fields: what it does, the motion in and out, the parts it needs (roles), the rules that make it work, what breaks it, and how to recognise it in a booklet.

mechanisms.does: Passes turning from one parallel shaft to another. Changes speed and force by the tooth ratio and reverses direction.
mechanisms.motion_out: rotation about a parallel axis, opposite direction
mechanisms.ratio: output turns = input turns x (driver teeth / driven teeth)

roles.bearings: round holes the shafts turn in

rules: Gears must be locked to their shafts (cross hole on axle).
Shafts must turn freely (round holes) and be held at the right distance: (teeth_a + teeth_b) / 16 holes for spur gears (e.g. 16+16 = 2 holes, 8+24 = 2, 12+20 = 2).
Each shaft needs support on two points or the gears push apart.
fails_when: Shaft in a cross hole of the frame (can't turn).
Distance wrong (teeth skip or jam).
Gear free on a round-hole part instead of locked to the axle.
mechanisms.recognise: Two gears side by side, teeth touching, on parallel axles.
mechanisms.verbs: DOES driver DRIVES driven; RATIO driver driven a/b; MESH driver.teeth driven.teeth

mechanisms.does: A gear between two others: carries turning across a gap and keeps the direction the same. Doesn't change the overall ratio.
mechanisms.motion_out: rotation, same direction as the first gear
mechanisms.ratio: overall = first / last teeth (the idler cancels out)

roles.idler: middle gear, often on a free-turning shaft

rules: Same spacing rule as gear_pair on both sides.
fails_when: Spacing wrong on either side.
mechanisms.recognise: Three or more gears in a row.
mechanisms.verbs: DOES a DRIVES idler; DOES idler DRIVES c

roles.driven: bevel gear on the perpendicular shaft

rules: Shaft axes must cross at a point; both gears sit 1 hole from the crossing for 12T/20T bevels.
fails_when: Gears not held tight against each other (they slip).
mechanisms.recognise: Two cone-shaped gears at right angles.
mechanisms.verbs: DOES a DRIVES b; RATIO a b x/y

mechanisms.does: A crown gear (teeth on its face) meshes with a normal gear at 90 degrees, or with a worm or spur gear in line.
rules: The other gear's teeth must reach the crown's face teeth.
fails_when: Gear too far from the face.
mechanisms.recognise: Gear with teeth on its flat side.

mechanisms.does: Big slow-down in one step, and self-locking: the gear can't turn the worm back, so the output holds its position (e.g. a boom stays up).
mechanisms.motion_out: slow rotation about a perpendicular axis
mechanisms.ratio: 1 / gear teeth (worm on a 24T gear: 24 turns of the worm = 1 turn of the gear)

roles.worm: worm gear locked on the input shaft
roles.thrust_stops: bushes or beams that stop the worm sliding along its shaft

rules: Worm shaft at 90 degrees to the wheel's shaft, worm touching the wheel's teeth.
The worm pushes along its own shaft: both sides need a stop or the worm slides out of mesh.
fails_when: No end stops: the worm walks along its shaft.
Worm too far from the wheel.
mechanisms.recognise: Spiral gear on a shaft crossing another gear.
mechanisms.verbs: DOES worm DRIVES wheel; RATIO worm wheel 1/N

mechanisms.does: Lets a whole upper structure rotate on a base. Big turntables have teeth so a gear can drive the rotation.
mechanisms.motion_in: rotation of a pinion (or by hand)
mechanisms.motion_out: rotation of the top half about the vertical axis
mechanisms.ratio: pinion teeth / ring teeth (e.g. 8T on 56T outer teeth = 1/7)

roles.base: fixed half, pinned to the chassis
roles.top: turning half, carries the upper structure
roles.pinion: gear on the upper structure meshing the ring's teeth

rules: Base fixed to the chassis on at least two points; top carries everything above.
The pinion's shaft must be fixed to the turning half so it walks round the ring.
fails_when: Pinion mounted on the fixed half (nothing turns).
mechanisms.recognise: Large ring with teeth between lower and upper machine.
mechanisms.verbs: DOES top SPINS_ON base; DOES pinion DRIVES ring

mechanisms.does: An axle that carries parts and turns, held from sliding by stops at both ends.
mechanisms.motion_out: same rotation along the whole shaft

roles.stops: bushes, axle-with-stop end, or a locked part on each side

rules: At least two round-hole bearings.
A stop on each side of the bearings.
fails_when: Shaft passes through a cross hole of a fixed part (it locks).
Missing stop: it slides out.
mechanisms.recognise: Axle with bushes on its ends.
mechanisms.verbs: DOES shaft SPINS_ON beam; DOES bush LOCKS shaft

mechanisms.does: Where a person turns the machine: a gear, wheel or knob on the end of an input shaft.
rules: Knob locked to the shaft; easy to reach from outside the model.
fails_when: Knob on a round-hole part (spins without turning the shaft).
mechanisms.recognise: Gear or round part on an exposed axle end.

mechanisms.does: Lets two parts swing about one axis.
mechanisms.motion_out: rotation about the hinge axis (limited range)

roles.pivot: frictionless pin or axle in round holes

rules: Use frictionless pins or axles for free swing; friction pins make it stiff.
fails_when: Friction pin where free movement is needed.
Pivot in a cross hole of one part AND a cross hole of the other (locked).
mechanisms.recognise: Two beams joined by one pin or axle.

mechanisms.does: Four bars joined by four hinges: moving one bar moves the others in a fixed way. Used to tip a stick or bucket as an arm moves.
rules: Four pivots, all free to turn.
Bar lengths decide the range and speed of the output.
fails_when: A pivot is locked; the linkage jams.
Lengths make it pass a dead point.
mechanisms.recognise: A loop of bars with pins at the corners.
mechanisms.verbs: DOES coupler HOLDS output; PATTERN linkage

mechanisms.does: A rod with a hinge at each end transfers push and pull between two parts that swing.

roles.end_hinges: angled connectors or pins at both ends

rules: Both ends must swing freely.
fails_when: One end fixed in a cross hole without a free pivot.
mechanisms.recognise: Long rod between two swinging parts.

mechanisms.does: A short arm on a shaft turns rotation into a back-and-forth swing (or the reverse).

roles.crank: short arm locked on a shaft
roles.link: bar from the crank pin to the moved part

rules: Crank locked to its shaft; the link turns on the crank's pin.
fails_when: Crank free on the shaft.
mechanisms.recognise: Short arm with a pin, a link on that pin.
mechanisms.verbs: DOES shaft CARRIES crank; DOES link SPINS_ON crank

mechanisms.does: Tread links wrapped round wheels: spreads weight, lets the machine roll or be driven.
mechanisms.motion_in: rotation of a drive wheel (or pushing)

roles.wheels: gears or sprockets the links mesh with

rules: Link count must fit the wheel spacing so the loop is tight.
Idler wheels on frictionless pins or free axles.
fails_when: Loop too loose (jumps off) or too tight (jams).
mechanisms.recognise: Chain of links round two or more gears.
mechanisms.verbs: MESH tread.teeth gear.teeth; DOES gear HOLDS track

mechanisms.does: Structure that keeps everything at the right distance. Not a moving mechanism, but every mechanism depends on it.

roles.joints: friction pins (2+ per joint stop twisting) or axles in cross holes

rules: A joint with one pin can swing: use two pins, an axle in cross holes, or close a triangle/rectangle.
Shafts' bearings must sit in the frame at the gear spacing.
fails_when: Single-pin joints where it must be stiff.
Open U shapes that spread under load.
mechanisms.verbs: DOES a SUPPORTS b; DOES pins LOCKS beam

mechanisms.does: Looks only: panels, hoses, lights. Carries little or no load, never part of a drive.
rules: Must not block moving parts.
fails_when: Rubs on a gear or link.

mechanisms.does: A hand pump pushes air through hoses and switches into a cylinder; the cylinder rod pushes or pulls a part. Used where a real machine would use hydraulics.
mechanisms.motion_out: push or pull of a cylinder rod

roles.switch: lever that chooses which cylinder or which side gets air
roles.cylinder: rod pushes when air enters one side

rules: Every outlet that is used needs a hose pushed fully onto the nozzle.
The cylinder must be pinned at both ends so its body and rod can swing.
Unused nozzles must be capped or left closed, or air escapes.
fails_when: A hose is loose or kinked.
A cylinder end is fixed in a cross hole (it cannot swing).
Hose too short for the swing of the part.
mechanisms.recognise: A pump, hoses, switches and a cylinder joined by air hoses.
